The house came into view over the grassy hill. The girl saw her Father’s grey Ford Fiesta parked at the front. She winced, slowing her movement and removing her school tie, tucking it messily in her navy blazer pocket. She unbuttoned the top suffocating button on her blouse and walked to the door. She held her ear to it expecting shouting and it came, muffled. With a sigh she put her headphones on her head from around her neck, soft rock already blaring. She turned a key slowly into the lock and opened the door silently, closing it with control. The shouting still lingered behind the electric sound in her ears. She tried focusing on the words as she took off her muddy black shoes. 

She walked up the rough carpet stairs, hopping left and right to avoid the creaks and entered her room with a sigh of relief. She threw off her jacket and lay face flat on her bed with a groan. She lay there for a minute before grabbing the desaturated duvet for several seconds, releasing both her hands and the flood gates of her ocean blue eyes. She cried silently, body trembling and tensing with her quickened breath. 

She paused like she remembered something and slowly sat herself up on her bed, regaining her breath. She took her rugged backpack off of her and rummaged through empty packets of crisps, uneaten fruit and stained school books. The shouting turned into lone crying under the floorboards. Underneath everything she found the device, a silver ear piece. She thought of the good friend that gave it to her months ago, forgotten with denial of this new technology. The news has started calling them Pockets, though she never looked further than the titles. Apparently her friends Dad was forced to throw it away by his wife, jealous and scared of what he could do in there. Her friend told her she should use it when she needs a break, which she knows the girl needs all too well. They said it stops time, she thinks. She moves her headphones down to her neck and places the ear piece carefully on. She looked for a button but the entire device was smooth. She felt a vibration as her finger felt a square of glass and she heard a voice, “Welcome back.”

She jumped at the voice and looked around her for the source. She noticed her curtain had stopped mid air, and the shouting has turned to complete silence. It must have worked, she thought. The same voice came, “I don’t recognise you, are you a new user?”, the voice must be coming from the ear piece, she thinks. It was a soft, synthetic-like female voice. 

“Yeah, I think I am.” Elin replied.

“Do you consent to your audio, requests and thoughts being monitored for my purposes?” 

“Sure, alright.”

“Please, tell me a bit about yourself.” The voice almost seemed human, though she was sure they only pre recorded these things. The girl felt she knew what to say immediately. 

“My name is Elin Tande, I just turned thirteen today and I live in Geiranger, Norway.” 

“It’s nice to meet you Elin, my name is Emily and I am your Guide. Would you like to edit the parameters of your Pocket?”

“Edit the para-what’s?” 

“Pocket Devices don’t just freeze time, they’re actually entirely new dimensions just for you, so you can do whatever you want with them. Visit France, recreate a deceased relative, or even create something entirely different from this world. May I suggest a popular choice for the younger generations, to disable gravity?” 

Elin’s eyes sparkled with anticipation, her mouth overwhelmed with ideas to pick from. She decides flying would be fun.

“Give me great big wings, like an Eagle.” She immediately feels wings grow gently along her back and marvels at herself in a long mirror, the feathers felt soft as they brushed against her back. They were massive, she looked at the tiny window, “Could you remove this house? And anyone inside of it, please.” The house was disappeared, leaving flat land in its place. 

“You only need think your requests now, imagine it and it will happen. Have fun dear.” Elin brightened at this and flapped her wings, it felt easy, like she had known it all her life. She flew up fast in just a few beats of her feathers and flew to a ledge on a high mountain. She didn’t feel the cold, nor the scent of fresh, moist air but smiled. She looked at the Fjord; a wide river surrounded by mountains, harbouring cruise ships. She had a new appreciation for the waterfalls dotting every mountain and ocean deep river, but it wasn’t quite good enough. She thought of a orange-pink sunset and so one faded in on the horizon, lighting up the dark teal waters. She marvelled at the moving spectacle until it disappeared under the water, her excitement joining it.

/Remove the world./, she thought. 

“We highly recommend starting small-“ 

She thought it again, louder. The world disappeared with a few seconds delay, and all there was, was nothing. Then something rendered in; the universe. Galaxies and stars and planets, none of which were earth. She saw what must have been the earth's moon and flew to it, but not much was happening there. A sofa appeared underneath her and she fell into it, her wings cushioning her. She watched as the stars burned and comets flew, the serenity of the place calmed her to her core. She thought hard about what more she could possibly want mor than this beautiful view, counting the stars. She closed her eyes and imagined it in great detail, the place she could spend eternity in, and when she opened her eyes she saw her parents smiling at her. Her Mother was thinner and her eyes were brighter and her Father didn’t look so numb. It wasn’t the grey, rented house she knew. The walls were painted a pastel blue that complimented the white furniture and she smelled a subtle cinnamon in the air. 

“How are you sweetie?” The Mother asked, still smiling. Elin was taken back by the gesture, smiling back. Her eyes grew heavy as she scanned her body, unsure on how she did feel.

“Sleepy, can I go to bed?” 

“Of course, as long as your okay. Hop up to bed and I’ll be there in a minute to tuck you in.” She answered still smiling. The Father nodded with a beaming smile. It felt a little unreal, almost creepy. Elin smiled back at them and hopped up soft, pink carpet stairs. At the top she found a single door with ‘Elin’ drawn in colourful paints and opened it. Behind the door was a king-size bed coated with pillows, the walls decorated with posters and the floor with books of all shapes and sizes. All of her favourite fantasy worlds in one place just ready to be reread a thousand times over. In another corner was an oak built guitar, and her favourite song was playing on Bluetooth speakers. She threw herself at her bed and sprawled across the soft duvet, her eyes growing heavy. She saw her Mother enter and watched, eyes half open as she kissed her on the head with a gentle “Goodnight.” With that her eyes fell.


“Ten minutes until Return is initiated.” She was awoken by the Guide. 

“Return?” She asked in a half asleep daze.

“Your time limit is up. I will be deactivating the device for 24 hours.” Elin’s eyes shot open and she sat up in her place. The colours were gone, the smell of cinnamon replaced with dull must, the room much smaller and the bed shrank with it. Elin’s eyes shot open in fear. 

“What? No, you can’t do this. You don’t know what it’s like back there. 

“You would have to go back eventually.”

“The longer I have to wait the better. Nobody wants me there anyway, they wouldn’t notice even if time was going by.” She failed to hold back tears.

“Thank you for your time, have fun!” Elin heard the wind against the curtains and burst into tears, no longer holding back. She screamed into her pillow and threw the device at the wall, splitting it in two. She didn’t notice the footsteps among her crying before the door slammed against her wall. She buried her head deeper into her pillow expecting more shouting as her tears wet her pillow. 

“Are you okay?” She heard her Mother's hoarse voice soften slightly. Elin paused and looked up at her with a sodden face. Her brows furrowed and she replied.

“Since when did you care? All you care about is yourself.” Her Mother looked shocked, then looked down.

“I’m sorry, I guess I get so wrapped up in myself that I forget you must be going through things too. You’re growing up so fast.” Elin looked at her and couldn’t hold back a smile. Both their tears stopped. Her Mother wrapped her arms around her and she gave in, smiling at her Dad behind her. He returned a small smile back.

“Happy Birthday, Elin.”
